concepts.angle: Symmetric race: two auto-assigned teams race the same puzzle at the same time, each in its own mirrored lane on the projected wall. Time-pressured shadow-building is the main skill. Riddle knowledge and drilled shadow skill from the rest of the session feed the race.
concepts.name: Lantern Run (سباق الفانوس)
concepts.one_liner: Two caravans, one wall: the room splits everyone into two teams, each team's lantern has to roll down its own mirrored lane to the Oasis, and the only road is the shadows your hands and props throw. The team that builds fastest, and answers its riddles best, gets home first.

concepts.name: Shadow Academy (أكاديمية الظل)
concepts.one_liner: The room splits everyone into teams on scan, then the teams learn, perform and guess hand-shadow animals on the wall while the camera checks every shadow against a target silhouette. Phones coach and guess, and each player earns stamps, ranks and a Shadow Book. The pitch is that you leave able to make real shadow animals with any torch and wall.

concepts.name: Lantern Keepers (Hurras al-Fanous), an UMBRA mode
concepts.one_liner: The room splits everyone into two teams (say Falcons and Oryx) that take turns: the Keepers hold real hand and prop shadows as windbreaks to protect a camp lantern, while the other team slings desert gusts at it from their phones. Quiz answers earn Flame Guards (for Keepers) or Boosts (for Raiders), and roles swap every 3 minutes so size and role differences even out.

concepts.angle: knowledge gates: an escape-room-style chain that two teams race through side by side, where a sand lock on some gates drains faster the more the team knows and the better its members cast shadows, but always opens eventually
concepts.name: Fanoos Gates
concepts.one_liner: Two teams, picked by the room, race a glowing lantern spark down side-by-side sand towers on the same wall. Real shadows are the bridges and the keys. Every riddle lock drains its sand faster the more the team knows and the better it casts, and it always opens in the end, so nobody is ever stuck or shut out.

concepts.name: Shadow Sahra (سهرة الظل)
concepts.one_liner: A 20-minute Gulf-evening game show on a wall of light, hosted by a talking lantern: the room splits everyone into two crews the moment they scan, then five short rounds (shadow fitting, a picture-first quiz that fuels power-ups, a bridge duel, silhouette charades, a finale) are won with real hand and prop shadows plus general knowledge.

concepts.name: Echo Dunes (Arabic: صدى الرمال, Sada al-Rimal)
concepts.one_liner: Each team builds the desert for the other team out of its own shadows. The wall records every wave, hold and swing for 12 seconds and replays it as glowing solid dunes. Then each team's lantern has to cross the dunes the rival team just made, so the players are the level designers and no level content ever runs out.

balance.reading:
WHAT WAS SAID: when the two teams are uneven, the team with one extra player is usually at a disadvantage compared with the team that has fewer. I read this three ways.

READING A (mechanical, which I ASSUME). The game's own mechanics and scoring cost the bigger team per head, so more players does not mean more output. Why this is plausible in UMBRA (the research is general, none of it was tested on a shared-beam phone game, kids or GCC groups, and the digest could not open the original papers, so treat the numbers as indicative):
- Social loafing / Ringelmann: per-person output falls as the group grows. The digest's figures are 100, 93, 85 and 49 percent of a solo effort at 1, 2, 3 and 8 people, but sources conflict on them. Ingham 1974 found that people who only believed others were pulling still dropped, so part of the loss is motivation, not just coordination. The biggest step is 1 to 2-3 people and later steps are small. Karau and Williams (1993, 78 studies) found loafing moderate and robust, and reduced when individual output is identifiable. Phone scores are identifiable, so it may be weaker here.
- Steiner: actual output = potential minus process loss. Extra heads add potential and also add losses.
- UMBRA-specific turn dilution. The beam is one finite shared surface and rounds have a fixed length, so each member of a team of 4 gets 25 percent of the airtime versus 33 percent for a team of 3. Extra hands crowd the beam, and the vision cannot tell whose shadow is whose.
- Per-capita scoring (mean of members, as Kahoot does) shows any loafing directly.
- All-or-nothing gates are conjunctive: at 90 percent per person the pass chance is 0.729, 0.656, 0.590 for 3, 4, 5 people, so a 4v3 split costs the bigger team about 7 points.

WHEN THE BIGGER TEAM IS INSTEAD AHEAD (so 'bigger = disadvantaged' cannot be a global rule):
- Sum scoring. Even with Ringelmann losses, total output n*p(n) still rises (about 1.22x going from 3 to 4 players).
- Pooled-answer knowledge rounds. P(at least one knower) = 1-(1-q)^n, which is 0.657, 0.760, 0.832 for n = 3, 4, 5 at q = 0.3.
- Beam rounds where the team has more people than beam seats: it can put its best casters in the beam.

WHAT MY OWN SIMULATION SHOWS (a model I assumed, not data): with per-head effort loss of 7 percent per extra person and a beam that holds 3 casters, the sign depends on the round type and the split size. With naive sum scoring the bigger team wins 58 percent at 4v3 and only 34 percent at 7v5. In per-capita parallel rounds it wins only 23 percent at 4v3 and 17 percent at 5v4. In beam rounds it wins 77 percent at 4v3. So the owner's intuition is true in some round types and false in others.

READING B (policy): the owner just wants the bigger team treated as the one to compensate, whatever the mechanics. Implemented as a flat bonus this is dangerous. An 8 percent flat bonus gives the bigger team 76 percent at 4v3 (teams balanced on true skill), because every 1 percent of bonus is worth about 3 points of win rate. If B is meant, the safe way is the same equal-seats rule below, which compensates by construction. A flat bonus may only exist as a small, disclosed, telemetry-tuned knob (at most 2 percent).

READING C (not assumed, a sanity hedge): the owner may have misspoken, since the usual intuition is that the smaller team is the disadvantaged one. One signed configuration value (the size-correction table below) can flip direction without a redesign.

RECOMMENDATION: assume A for the mechanism, and fix it in the game's structure, not with multipliers. Give both teams the same number of scoring seats (the extra player rotates out into a real Spotter role), score per capita, and give equal turns. In the sim this holds the bigger team at 49.8 to 50.3 percent on 4v3, 5v4, 6v5 and 7v5 with true-skill balance, and it stays at about 50 whether the true per-head loss is 0, 3.5, 7 or 11 percent. Multipliers need the exact loss and break otherwise. Honest limit: equal seats only removes the part of the penalty that comes from the number of people ACTING. If loafing is driven by total team size even for benched members, the bigger team is still disadvantaged: 4v3 falls to 42 percent if half the effect is of that kind and 34 percent if all of it is. So also log per-capita output by team size and keep the signed correction knob, off by default.

At the PERSON level the owner is right in any case: on an even-seat design a member of a team of 4 plays 3 of 4 rounds (75 percent; 5v4 gives 80 percent). So the Spotter role must feel like a promotion, not a bench.

ONE QUESTION TO CONFIRM WITH THE OWNER: 'when you say disadvantaged, do you mean they lose more, or they get less airtime per person?' The design covers both, but the answer decides how much effort goes into the Spotter role.
balance.defaults:
SHIP IN V1 (default configuration):
- The room assigns teams; no player choice. Team count: 2 teams from 4 to 10 players; N of 1 = solo vs the Night; N of 2-3 = co-op vs the Night; 3-4 teams only once the game concept supports lanes (maxTeams = 2 until then); above 16 players = audience. Team sizes differ by at most 1, maximum 5.
- Assignment: optional age-band tap, 45-60 s warm-up, rating = (2*prior + measurements) / (2 + count), exhaustive min-cost split with random choice among near-ties, team reveal, ONE snake re-draft after round one (at most ceil(N/4) moves, gain at least 0.03), teams locked for a 3-round act, shuffle-or-keep vote at each act break with a repeat-pair penalty of 0.08.
- Fairness: equal active seats (S = smaller team's size) with least-active-first rotation and a Spotter with NO scoring effect (a size-independent team ping); per-capita mean scoring with par-normalised player contributions; individual answers averaged in knowledge rounds; share-of-members gates; equal turns and ABBA order in turn-based rounds.
- Scoring: P = 100 * Q * F * C with F = 1.00 and C = the disclosed Moonrise boost, 1 + min(0.10, 0.25*g), for the trailing team only. Flat awards identical for both teams.
- Late joiner to the smallest team at the next boundary; 60 s grace for a disconnect; token reconnect to the same slot; rebalance only when the gap is 2 or more.
- Naming: fixed name sets with Arabic and Latin forms, Okabe-Ito colours plus emblem shape and pattern, hand-shadow animal as the team emblem.

LEAVE OFF IN V1 (kept as config and telemetry only): the size-based multiplier (F table), flat bonus, ghost player, neutral Moonkeeper, households, age-based score multiplication (never), 3-4 teams until the concept supports them.

TELEMETRY TO LOG FROM DAY ONE (no personal data): per round, team size, active seats, per-capita output by round type; Spotter uplift; win rate by size gap; blowout rate; re-draft moves and their effect; rematch rate. Use 6-10 real playtest rooms to set the F table per round type and to decide whether the signed correction is needed. Run the first playtests with families, with a mixed-age room and an adults-only room.

ONE QUESTION TO ASK THE OWNER: do you mean the bigger team loses more, or that its members get less airtime? The design handles both, but the answer decides how much effort the Spotter role gets.

EFFORT (assumes 12-15 focused hours per week and 1 dev-day = 6 hours, i.e. 2-2.5 dev-days per calendar week; this is my estimate, not a measurement): assignment + warm-up + reveal about 2.5 dev-days; seats, rotation and scoring 1.5; late join, leave, reconnect and rebalance 1.0; telemetry and config table 0.5; unit and e2e tests (4v3, 5v4, 3 teams, leavers) 1.0. Total about 6.5 dev-days, roughly 3 calendar weeks. The reference code in the design-work folder (assign.js, about 270 lines, plus its tests) already implements and tests team count, the cost function, the exhaustive split, snake draft, late-join placement, rebalance and re-draft, so porting it should save about a day. Playtesting with 6-10 groups is extra and calendar-bound.
balance.simulation:
WHAT I BUILT AND RAN. Folder: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-newapp/dfe43cf3-95b2-5df4-8871-9b3a8798b31d/scratchpad/design-work/teams-fairness/ (files: rng.js, assign.js [team-count policy, cost J, exhaustive 2-team split, snake draft, swap search, late-join placement, rebalance, re-draft], engine.js [world model and rule sets], sim.js [experiments 1-7], selftest.js [946 checks, all pass], out_exp*.txt [raw outputs]). Reproduce: node selftest.js; node sim.js exp2 (about 90 s); other experiments exp1, exp2b, exp3, exp4, exp5, exp6, exp7. Nothing was written to /home/user/newapp; other files already in design-work belong to other work and were not touched.

THE MODEL IS AN ASSUMPTION, NOT DATA. Per-head effort p(n) = 1 - 0.07*(n-1) (Ringelmann-style, floored at 0.35). The beam holds 3 casters at full value and extra casters add 25 percent each (diminishing returns per extra player). Skill: lognormal around kid 0.60, teen 0.85, adult 1.00 par with a within-band SD of 0.25; per-round noise 0.30; 15 percent of players skip the age tap. Room mix: 50 percent family camp, 25 percent adults only, 25 percent youth group. A session is 5 rounds: BEAM, PAR (parallel phone), KNOW (5 questions), GATE (3 gates), BEAM. Round points are normalised to a par of 100. The bigger team is whichever has more players. I report the bigger team's win rate (50 is fair) with 95 percent CIs over rosters.

A. HEAD-COUNT BIAS ISOLATED (teams balanced on TRUE skill, which the product cannot do; 1,500 rosters x 60 sessions, CI +/-0.4-0.5; 4v4 control = 50.1):
- Naive sum scoring: 58.4 (4v3), 49.6 (5v4), 43.8 (6v5), 33.8 (7v5). The sign flips with size.
- Per-capita mean only: 53.3, 46.3, 40.1, 25.9.
- Size multiplier from the loafing curve (delta 0.07): 78.1, 77.4, 75.3, 61.7. With delta halved: 65.5, 60.6, 56.2, 57.8. Overshoots badly.
- Flat 8 percent bonus (Reading B literal): 76.1, 72.8, 69.2, 54.7.
- RECOMMENDED equal active seats + rotation, mean scoring, Spotter with no score effect: 50.2, 50.0, 50.3, 49.9. With catch-up added: 50.3, 50.1, 50.3, 49.8.
- Same but the Spotter adds 2 percent: 56.4, 56.9, 57.8, 57.1. Sensitivity of the bigger team's win rate to the Spotter bonus (4v3 / 5v4 / 7v5): 0% = 49.8/49.9/49.9; 2% = 55.7/57.0/57.3; 5% = 64.4/66.5/67.7; 10% = 76.4/79.7/81.5. So about +3 points per +1 percent.
Per round type (4v3, bigger team win rate, true-skill balance): naive sums PAR 96.8, BEAM 77.4, KNOW 79.3, GATE 22.4; mean-only PAR 22.7, BEAM 77.4, KNOW 51.0, GATE 36.3; recommended equal seats 50.7, 50.7, 50.1, 47.7. At 7v5 the recommended rule gives 49.9, 49.9, 49.8, 48.7 against naive 92.6, 37.6, 75.4, 6.7. GATE leans 1-2 points toward the smaller team under equal seats (likely a concavity effect of the success curve).

B. REALISTIC ASSIGNMENT (age-band prior plus one noisy warm-up measurement; 2,500 rosters x 40 sessions, CI +/-1.2; 4v4 control 51.3 within the same roster draw): recommended rule 50.6, 51.1, 50.8, 51.3 for 4v3, 5v4, 6v5, 7v5, so within about one point of the control. Naive sum 57.7, 51.1, 45.8, 37.3. Size multiplier 71.3, 71.2, 69.0, 59.2. Flat bonus 69.8, 67.7, 64.5, 54.2. Spotter 2 percent: 55.0, 56.0, 56.0, 56.6.

C. THREE TEAMS (4/4/3, 3,000 rooms x 30 sessions): share of wins for the three-player team is 26.8 percent under naive sums, 31.3 under mean scoring and 33.2 under the recommended rules (fair = 33.3); the two four-player teams get 33.6 and 33.1.

WHERE MY RULES DO NOT FIX IT (be careful with these):
1. LOPSIDED ROOMS ARE NOT FIXED BY ANY SIZE RULE. In the realistic setup the per-room win chance has an SD of about 28-29 points and roughly two thirds of rooms are 'blowouts' (the favoured side's win chance outside 35-65 percent), the same as in the 4v4 control (SD 30). The cause is skill-estimate noise, not head-count: the true skill gap between teams averages 0.15 par at 4v3 (join-order alternation and a random split are equal at 0.165) and only 0.12 after age-band balancing plus a warm-up; a perfect-information balance would be 0.018. Re-draft after round one drops the SD to 19.7 points and blowouts to 51 percent; three warm-up measurements instead of one give 24.0 and 60 percent; a stronger catch-up (cap 20 percent / 30 percent) barely helps (27.6 / 26.7). All three together give 19.6 and 51 percent. If skill spread is 0.15 instead of 0.25 or the game is luckier (noise 0.5), blowouts fall to about 36 percent with all fixes (41-44 percent with the less lucky settings), still not small. These magnitudes depend on my two assumed constants.
2. EQUAL SEATS ONLY REMOVES THE PENALTY FROM ACTING PLAYERS. If loafing is driven by total team size (benched members included), the bigger team is still disadvantaged even with equal seats: at delta 0.07, 4v3 falls to 42.3 percent (half the effect) and 34.4 percent (all of it); 5v4 to 39.8 and 30.0; 7v5 to 26.4 and 9.4. Whether this happens is unknown; telemetry from real rooms is required, hence the signed per-round-type size table.
3. Multipliers are fragile: mean-only scoring at 4v3 goes from 70.8 percent (no loafing) to 54.0 (delta 0.07) to 39.0 (delta 0.11); the full size factor goes from 89.5 to 78.8 to 66.4. Equal seats with the penalty on acting players only stays at 49.3-50.5 across all four loafing strengths and all three splits tested (4v3, 5v4, 7v5).
4. Not simulated: late joiners, leavers and reconnects (only unit-tested for sizes and bounded moves), households, the ghost and Moonkeeper variants, more than 3 teams, real humans, kids, or any real vision output. Assignment scale is checked only to 16 players. There is no evidence here about GCC groups.

REPEAT PAIRS: without a repeat penalty 52-60 percent of teammate pairs repeat after a reshuffle; with 0.08 it falls to 39-43 percent, about the same as a random shuffle (43-45 percent), while the skill gap stays at 0.10-0.12 vs 0.14-0.17 for a random shuffle.

BOTTOM LINE: head-count bias is solved in the model by design (equal seats), cheaply and robustly; real unfairness from uneven teams then reduces to the unknown spill-over and to the much larger skill-balance problem, which this design reduces but does not remove.

judgeRecommendations.lens: Veteran party-game designer and playtester judging how each concept feels at a camp table: laughter and tension, replay pull, 4-to-grandparent inclusion, shareable moments, and whether skill and knowledge arise from the play itself rather than a quiz bolted on. Solo buildability and real-hardware vision risk are weighed because the owner builds alone this winter. All scores are my judgement from the written designs. Nothing was playtested, and the fairness numbers rest on the spec's assumed model.
judgeRecommendations.recommendation:
Build ONE game: Echo Dunes' build-prove-cross loop on Lantern Run's lane and seat chassis, with a Silhouette Charades act break, a Light Check/Curtain Call bookend, and Predict and Test plus Oasis Gate as the knowledge beats. The room draws the teams with the spec's assign(): optional age tap, Light Check as the rating, exhaustive split, 20-second reveal, one re-draft after round one. Sessions are three-round acts. In Dunes rounds the bigger team's extra player rotates into a Spotter with zero scoring effect. The Charades round is turn-based, so everyone performs and there is no Spotter. That gives the bigger team's members enough airtime to feel the Spotter role is a promotion.

Why this order: Echo Dunes wins on fun, replay and shadow necessity, and has the best solo-build economics because the players author the levels. It is weak on knowledge and has a rule-load problem. Shadow Academy supplies what Echo Dunes lacks (natural knowledge, a skill people can see themselves gain, 4-to-grandparent inclusion) but is too risky to be the trunk, because template matching on real hands is unproven. Lantern Run supplies the fairness and the safest engine reuse. The rest are quarries.

Build order: (1) Day 1 is a real-projector test with a cheap mini and a bedsheet, covering recording noise and echo alignment. If it fails, nothing else matters. (2) Slice 1 (about 12-14 days): teams and draw, mirrored lanes with seats, Classic Dunes, Light Check, round-1 Build+Cross only. (3) Slice 2 (about 5-6 days): Charades human-judged with 6-8 animals, plus Predict and Test. (4) Fast-follow: camera-verified stamps, Oasis Gate, Blind-free extras. My total is roughly 17-20 dev-days from the concepts' own estimates, so a mid-December soft launch rather than 15 Nov. Treat that as unproven.

Before finalising, ask the owner one thing: when he says the bigger team is disadvantaged, does he mean it loses more, or that each member gets less airtime? The design covers both, but the answer decides how much effort the Spotter role gets. Be honest that equal seats only removes the penalty from acting players. Log per-capita output by team size in 6-10 real playtests and keep the signed correction off by default.
merge: CHASSIS FROM LANTERN RUN: mirrored half-wall lanes with a neutral centre margin and a shadow-area cap (about 25%), half-time swap of sides, seat table from the smaller team (S=min(3,smaller): 2 casters + 1 pilot, or 1+1 at S=2), the size-independent coach/spotter ping, one team clock, and 8 fixed answer slots with a continuous gauge (never rounded or averaged per player). This is the spec's equal-seats rule already written as a game. Add the spec's assign(), warm-up rating, re-draft after round one and 20-second reveal on top.

CORE LOOP FROM ECHO DUNES: build a trap (record, then layer a second take), prove it yourself, then cross the rival's trap. Live shadows are black ('now') and echoes are saturated colour ('then'). Round 1 is Build+Cross only, with a Friendly mode where Prove is optional. Best-Trap vote with picture stickers, the youngest player breaking ties, and a silhouette-only best-trap replay. This replaces hand-authored courses, so content never runs out.

SILHOUETTE CHARADES FROM SHADOW ACADEMY as the act-break round and the skill-and-knowledge engine: the performer sees a picture card for 5 s, then makes it from memory, and teammates guess from a per-phone tiered picture grid. Accuracy over speed, one icon-chip clue, a one-sentence fact, and missed animals come back later. Everyone performs (equal heats, the smaller team's repeat goes to its least-exposed member), so the Dunes Spotter gets compensating airtime here. Ship it human-judged first, with the camera only checking clarity once real captures set par values. Use the hand-shadow animal as the team emblem at the reveal, tier-0 body shapes (Tree, Tent) for the youngest, Buddy Pose cards, and a Pocket Zoo take-home card.

KNOWLEDGE THAT BECOMES A SHADOW ACT: Predict and Test as the finale (phones predict, a Hand proves it live) from Fanoos Gates and Shadow Sahra, and Oasis Gate (the right answer picks which plate to cover) from Echo Dunes. Keep the principle that every round is clearable with zero knowledge. Drop the separate quiz phases.

SKILL BOOKENDS: a 45-60 s Light Check (ring fit by coverage minus spill, small then big) as the warm-up. It doubles as the spec's rating measurement for the draw, with the same ring sizes counterbalanced in a closing Curtain Call from Shadow Sahra, plus a Most Improved award measured against the player's own baseline so a child can win. Persist Fanoos Gates's Light Craft rungs (size window, steady hold, orientation, compose) on the phone and wall as the long-term ladder.

SMALL BORROWS: announced forecast cards, same for both teams in ABBA order, plus honest near-miss wording ('your bridge was one hand-width low') from Lantern Keepers. Spotter role framed as a promotion (full-board view, team emote, assist badge) with zero scoring effect. Use only the spec's single disclosed catch-up (at most 10%) and a signed size correction that is off by default.
cut: Lantern Keepers' slingshot attack/defend split: half the team plays a phone aiming game with no shadows, defenders must hold poses for about 90 s, live saves are latency-luck, the shade-budget filter is unproven, and it needs World physics rework. Keep only forecast cards and near-miss wording.

Shadow Sahra as a five-round game-show shell, including its separate Bridge Duel and Showdown (33 days, six rule sets). Harvest Light Check, Curtain Call and Predict-the-Light only. The host mascot is a cheap optional extra, not a requirement.
Fanoos Gates' sand-lock gate chain and 270-item quiz bank: dead waiting time, school feel, private-only feedback, 27 days. Keep Predict and Test, Whose shadow? and the craft ladder.

Lantern Run's separate pit-stop quiz that pays Oil before each leg, and its 4 hand-tuned course recipes. The quiz is a tax rather than part of the game, and authoring plus hand-size tuning is exactly the work Echo Dunes removes.

Echo Dunes' fixed 2-caster rule (a 2-person team has no pilot), the captain's 1.5 vote (a hidden size correction), the pre-round Wisdom Glow riddle as the main knowledge mechanic, Blind Dunes, the 12-trap Ghost Caravan library, and 3-4 team round-robin judging in v1. Use the spec's solo-vs-the-Night and audience-judge overflow instead.

Shadow Academy's Open Studio look-alike suggestions (the matcher cannot separate look-alikes), the 3-lane layout, the Last Light finale and share card in v1, per-animal par thresholds before real-hand captures, and a 20-animal launch (ship 8 and add to 12-20 later). Also drop animal pairs that look alike (Rabbit with Gazelle).

Every concept's own team balancer, underdog knob and age-tier tap (star-size, hand-size, age icon): replace them with the spec's single assign(), one optional kid/teen/adult tap and one disclosed catch-up. Any flat bonus for the bigger team (Reading B taken literally) overshoots badly in the spec's sim.

judgeRecommendations.lens: Pragmatic indie engineering lead. Every score is a judgment from the concept write-ups and the research digest, not a measurement. Nothing here was tested on a real projector, and the fairness numbers come from the spec's own simulation, which uses assumed constants. Solo feasibility is scored hardest. It covers dev-days against 2 to 2.5 dev-days per week, reuse of the existing engine, content burden, vision accuracy needed (blob-level shadows are tolerant; finger-level shape discrimination is not), balance-tuning surface, and whether a real-hardware playtest fits in about 5 dev-days over two weeks. Fairness is scored on how natively the concept already gives both teams the same number of scoring seats, per-capita mean scoring and equal turns, as the team-balance spec requires. Weighted ranking: solo feasibility x2, fairness x1.5, the other eight criteria x1. Timeline from 11 Oct 2026: about 11 dev-days to Kuwait's likely 15 Nov start, about 15 to 19 to 5 Dec, and about 30 to 15 Jan. Arabic/RTL, payments and the offline relay are not counted in any concept's build_days, so every real ship date is later than quoted.
judgeRecommendations.recommendation:
Build Lantern Run as the chassis and merge a short list of parts into it. Do not build any of the other five as a standalone product this winter.

Why Lantern Run: it has the lowest risk and the most prototype evidence. It tolerates blob-level shadows, its fairness already matches the team-balance spec (equal seats, one clock, size-neutral quiz slots), and Slice 1 (about 10 dev-days) is the only slice that fits the 15 Nov Kuwait start. Its weakness is thin knowledge integration and a small course library, and the merge list above fixes both with cheap parts: Predict and Test, and later the Echo Leg.

What to build in the next two weeks (about 5 dev-days at 12 to 15 h a week), in this order:
1. Day 1: a real-projector vision test. Use a cheap mini projector and a 400-lumen unit on a sheet or tent wall, camera at least 30 degrees off-axis and low, hands and props, with a lantern or fire in view. Everything else depends on this result. If shadows are not clean, fall back to a single lane against a ghost team.
2. Days 2 to 3: port the team module. That is the assign() seam, the picture-tap join, the warm-up rating, the reveal, and the 2 Casters + Pilot + Coach seats. Test 4v3 and 5v4 headlessly with the sim camera.
3. Days 4 to 5: a lanes module with the World refactor from constants to per-instance dimensions. Build one tuned course with gaps of 180 px or more, and race it first-lantern-home.
4. Then playtest with two real families. Log per-capita output and win rate by team size from the first session.

After that, Slice 2 (Craft Drill before and after, Pit Stops with Oil, the Predict and Test finale, awards) is about 10 more dev-days. The merged game is about 21 to 22 dev-days in total, so honestly plan a mid-December soft-launch. Arabic/RTL, payments and the offline relay come on top.

Spike Echo's record and replay only if the day-1 vision test is clean, and only for 1 to 2 days. Run a separate 3 to 4 day matcher spike for hand-shadow animals (Shadow Academy) only if the owner wants the hand-shadow story, because it carries the highest vision risk and can quietly consume the whole window.

On the owner's team requirement: the room assigns everyone and nobody picks a team. Fairness comes from the spec's structure, not from bonuses. Use equal scoring seats, a rotating Spotter or Coach with zero score effect, and per-capita scoring. Any size correction stays a disclosed knob at 2% or less that can flip sign, so the 8% to 17% allowances in the concepts do not ship. Uneven-team balance will not fix lopsided rooms by itself. Skill-estimate noise is the bigger problem, so add the one-time re-draft after leg 1 as soon as the basic assign() works.

Questions to confirm with the owner: when he says the bigger team is disadvantaged, does he mean it loses more or that each member gets less airtime? The design covers both, but the answer decides how much effort goes into making the Coach role feel like a promotion. A second question is which countries to sell in first. Kuwait's season dates are unannounced, and the payment route depends on the owner's nationality and licence.
merge: CHASSIS: Lantern Run's mirrored two-lane race. It has the only prototype evidence (identical 3.18 s runs in both lanes), the highest engine reuse, blob-level shadow tolerance, and a Slice 1 of about 10 dev-days that lands near 15 Nov. Keep exactly 4 legs so tent-swap at half-time balances sides.

TEAM MODULE FROM THE SPEC, BUILT FIRST: port assign.js (the roughly 270-line reference with 946 passing checks) behind one assign() seam. Join with a nickname and an optional kid, teen or adult tap, no team picker. The Craft Drill is the warm-up rating, then comes the exhaustive min-cost split, a 20 s reveal, and Okabe-Ito colour plus emblem plus hand-shadow animal. Seats are S = min(3, smaller team): 2 Casters and 1 Pilot, extras are Coach with a size-independent ping and zero score effect (spotterScoreEffect = 0), least-active-first rotation, and a one-time re-draft after leg 1 (at most ceil(N/4) moves, only if J improves by at least 0.03) because lopsided rooms, not headcount, are the biggest unfairness left. Spotters still answer pit-stop cards, so the Coach role is a promotion, not a bench.

KNOWLEDGE, CHEAP VERSION: Lantern Run's Pit Stop (8 answer slots per team dealt round-robin, tiered cards, accuracy not speed, one-sentence 'did you know') because it is size-neutral by simulation. Add Fanoos Gates' principle that knowledge only shortens a wait and never blocks, applied as Oil that cancels a restart. Upgrade the finale pit stop to a 'Predict and Test' card (from Fanoos Gates and Shadow Sahra's Predict-the-Light): phones predict, a Caster does it live, the camera measures the area change. It is procedural, needs no extra questions, and makes the real shadow the answer key.

SKILL PROOF: Lantern Run's opening and closing Craft Drill, with Shadow Sahra's Curtain Call presentation ('Maha 7.2 s to 3.4 s') and Fanoos Gates' lantern rungs, stored on the phone with no accounts. Use only blob-level targets (Moon, Bridge bar, Ramp, Giant vs Tiny). Add at most two or three clearly distinct hand-shadow animals as optional drill targets from Shadow Academy, so the hand-shadow story is tested cheaply.

CONTENT ENGINE, AS POST-LAUNCH MODULE: Echo Dunes' record-and-replay as one bonus leg ('Echo Leg') where the rival team's recorded shadows become your obstacles. It uses setShadow(live OR echo), and it fixes the thin-course-library risk. First prove the clean-recording spike (1 to 2 days) on a real projector.

FAIRNESS DETAILS: one team clock (Lantern Run), mean scoring with ABBA turn order, share-of-members gates (never p^n), the disclosed catch-up capped at about 10% and based on score gap, never team size, and a log of win rate and per-capita output by team size from day one. The spec's single signed size-correction knob replaces all concept-specific knobs.

SMALL TOUCHES: Shadow Sahra's host character (a talking Fanoos lantern with about 60 recorded lines), Fanoos Gates' 'walk-out' so the losing lane never stalls under 20 s, Lantern Run's Underdog Oil as the disclosed catch-up, and Shadow Academy's off-by-default household link for a parent and a small child.
cut: Lantern Keepers as a whole: the ballistic SiegeWorld mode, the shade-budget filter, slingshot phone rounds and the forecast cards. It does not reuse the puzzle levels, has the worst knowledge integration, and its core constants are all unproven. Keep only the idea that role swaps drive replay.
Shadow Sahra as a five-round show: the show director, Copycat, Shape-Gate Showdown, awards voting and the 33-day plan. Keep Light Check, Curtain Call and Predict-the-Light as modules only.
Fanoos Gates' chamber chain, Sand Lock engine, the 270-item three-tier question bank, tier drift, the Caravan ghost lane, and stencil tiers beyond a ring and a bar.

Echo Dunes' Blind Dunes, Oasis Gate, the 3 to 4 team judge rotation, 'Easy Dunes' assist and the captain's 1.5x vote. The vote is a size-dependent power that contradicts zero Spotter effect. Defer the whole mode to a post-launch spike.
Shadow Academy's Charades, Open Studio, Last Light, the 20-animal set, Book restore codes, and any pair of look-alike animals, until a real-projector spike shows the matcher can separate them.

Every concept-specific size knob: sizeAllowanceSec of +/-6 s (about 8% of a leg), sizeBonus of 0.90 to 1.10, sizeAdj of +/-10 s of sand (about 17%), sizeComp of 1.5 s per extra head (about 12%), and Underdog tokens per extra player. The spec's simulation shows about 3 points of win rate per 1% of bonus, so these overshoot by 3 to 10x. Replace them with the spec's single signed correction, clamped to 2% and off by default.
3 to 4 team heats and a maxTeams above 2 in v1, the neutral Moonkeeper, the ghost player and the F table, all per the spec's ship list.

Physical props kit and a local-gateway payment build this season: ship the printable prop sheet as a free PDF in the unlock. Arabic/RTL, the offline relay and payments are still real work and sit outside every concept's day count.

judgeRecommendations.lens: Gulf family-entertainment publisher: what parents and camp hosts would buy and recommend, Arabic/English accessibility (picture-first, low text, content-review cost), how fair the two teams perceive the game to be, uniqueness against existing party games (Jackbox, Mkhmkh-style quizzes, Arabic charades apps), and whether it demos in a 15-second Snapchat/Instagram clip. All scores are my judgement from the concept write-ups. The research digest was read through search summaries, camp projector demand is unproven, and nothing has been tested on a real projector.
judgeRecommendations.recommendation:
Build one game: a Lantern Run race (mirrored lanes, room-assigned teams, equal seats with a Spotter) whose gates are opened by a Shadow Academy hand-shadow craft, with picture-first silhouette riddles deciding what to cast, and an Echo round held back for January or Ramadan.

Shadow Academy scores highest on market appeal (clip, parent pitch, mixed age). Lantern Run is the safest to build and the fairest to watch. Sequence them by risk. First, spend the first 1-2 dev-days on a real-projector test with a cheap mini and a 400-lumen unit on a sheet or tent wall. If hands and animals read cleanly, the Academy drill is cheap to graft on. If they do not, the coarse bridge and ring mechanics of Lantern Run still ship.

Slice 1 (about 10 dev-days): auto-teams, equal seats, mirrored lanes, 2 courses, the Ghost Caravan solo mode, and the Wave Hello echo tutorial. At 2-2.5 dev-days a week from 11 Oct, that lands near Kuwait's likely 15 Nov start, but only just. Show it to 5-10 real camp groups, since camp projector demand is unproven. Slice 2 (about 10 more days) adds the Craft Drill with 6-8 animals and before/after, the Pit Stop riddles with Riddle Fork, and awards, landing around mid-December before the school-break peak. Charades, Echo round and Ramadan skin follow for February and Eid.

Arabic RTL (3-5 days), the payments checkout (2-6 days, merchant-of-record route) and offline or hotspot play are not in any concept's day count and must be added. The Spotter role must feel like a promotion, because the bigger team's members still play only 75% of rounds at 4v3. Ask the owner one question: 'when you say disadvantaged, do you mean they lose more, or get less airtime per person?'. Ship F = 1.00 and log per-capita output by team size from the first playtest.

Marketing and price (my proposal, not market-tested): lead with the clip of a hand making a falcon and a lantern crossing a bridge made of shadows. Offer a free tier (Ghost Caravan plus 2 courses, no ads), a Founder host pass near KWD 3.5 / SAR 39 / AED 39 with guests free, and a camp-operator season licence later.
merge: CHASSIS from Lantern Run: two mirrored lanes with the same seeded course, tents swapped at half-time, one team clock, a shadow-area cap and a neutral centre margin. It is the most visibly fair format, reuses the engine most, and Slice 1 is about 10 dev-days.

TEAM LAYER from the team-balance spec, unchanged: no team picker, one assign() function, age-band tap, 45-60 s Shadow Check warm-up, exhaustive min-cost split, 20 s reveal, one snake re-draft after round one, shuffle-or-keep vote at act breaks, equal active seats with a rotating Spotter who has zero score effect, per-capita mean scoring, F = 1.00, maxTeams = 2. Use the Okabe-Ito colours, the Arabic-and-Latin name sets, and a hand-shadow-animal emblem for each team.

SKILL SPINE and CLIP from Shadow Academy: a Craft Drill of 6-8 distinct launch animals and shapes (avoid look-alike pairs), with the wall's match ring and a before/after per player, a Shadow Book of stamps on each phone, and Buddy Pose for child plus parent. This is the 15-second clip and the line a parent repeats.

KNOWLEDGE from the best of three: Lantern Run's picture-first tiered Pit Stop cards (same topic, own tier, accuracy not speed, 8 answer slots per team), Fanoos Gates' Predict-and-Test, and Academy's one-sentence 'Did you know?'. Promote Riddle Fork into v1 so the right answer names the shape the team must cast. That makes knowledge the shadow act, not a bolt-on quiz.

CHEAP ECHO from Echo Dunes: use the 45 s 'Wave Hello' ghost-echo tutorial now (a ghost of your own wave beside your live hand). Hold the full record-and-cross 'Echo round' for a January or Ramadan expansion.

FRAMING from Shadow Sahra: Fanoos the lantern as host, the Curtain Call before/after recap, peer-voted awards so every team leaves with something, an Express length for Ramadan evenings, and a Camp Log on the host device.
FREE DEMO from Lantern Run and Echo Dunes: the Ghost Caravan solo and co-op mode for 1-3 players, used as the free tier and the demo clip, with the Night opponent from the team spec.
cut: Lantern Keepers as a whole: the attack/defend structure, phone slingshot, forecast and boost layers, and the shade-budget filter. Shadows are not essential to half the room, the fairness is invisible, and the 'Raiders' framing is awkward for family buyers.

Fanoos Gates' full chain: the sand-lock engine, 270 bilingual items and 8-9 lane-sized chambers (27 dev-days, school feel, head-on competition with Mkhmkh). Keep only Predict-and-Test and the always-opens principle.
Shadow Sahra's five-round show and its 33 days. Take the framing, not the structure. Cut the auto-judged Predict-the-Light and a large quiz bank.
Echo Dunes' Prove-or-void rule, Blind Dunes, 3-4 team round-robin, and player-made traps shared as replays in v1 (rule load, uneven trap difficulty, rude-gesture risk).
Shadow Academy's Charades, Open Studio, Last Light, third lane, share card and any look-alike classification, until the real-projector test passes and the launch is out.

Team-spec options kept off in v1: household linking, ghost player, neutral Moonkeeper, flat bonus for the bigger team (Reading B taken literally), any size multiplier other than 1.00, 3-4 teams, and the Moonrise catch-up beyond a small, disclosed boost.

Anything chance-based or dark-pattern: streaks, countdown offers, loot boxes, push notifications, ads and chat. They are unnecessary under a host-buys-once model, and regulators in Kuwait and KSA accepted chat-free play.

criticVerdict:
Not ready to call final. The design does what the owner asked on the main points. Teams are assigned with no player choice, uneven rooms are handled by structure (equal seats plus one team clock) and not by bonuses, and the doc is candid that fairness, vision and demand are unproven. But I found two blockers, a pile of major issues and several internal contradictions.

Blockers:
1. The night-themed skins cannot work with the existing vision engine, because dark pixels read as shadows.
2. The dates and scope the owner is asked to approve (decision 4) leave out items the doc itself says are required before taking money.

The headline fairness number (50.2% for the bigger team) is true by construction of the model, not evidence about the race format. The "addictive" goal is not supported by the v1 that actually ships. The v1 inherits the two weakest scores of the chosen concept (knowledge 4.0, replay 5.3), and every graft that fixes them lands after the Founder build.

On "do real shadows matter":
- Yes in the Leg, the Light Check and Predict and Test.
- No in Pit Stop and human-judged Charades.
- A big prop makes shadows easy to fake, and the area cap that is meant to stop this is unspecified.

Engine facts I checked in /home/user/newapp/umbra:
- Vision runs at most at 20 Hz (host/app.js visionTick).
- It uses a 2-frame debounce (core/vision-core.js).
- The grid is 160x90 cells over a 960x540 world (6 px per cell).
- palette.js uses a white background and enforces "no dark ink".
- MAX_PLAYERS is 8.
- The relay is stateless and forwards inputs to the host.

issues.where: Section 11 skins (Desert Night default, Night Caravan, Majlis Night, Ramadan Lanterns), Section 3 emblems and Al Sadu borders, Section 5 Pit Stop silhouettes, Section 2 wall text
issues.problem: The design assumes night and dark art. The engine forbids it. umbra/public/js/game/palette.js sets the background to #ffffff and enforces, by test, that every drawn colour keeps one channel near full, because dark ink is read as shadow. The detector marks a cell as shadow when it is below 0.3 of the calibrated white (onT). A dark night sky, black or dark Al Sadu borders, black silhouettes and dark text would all become solid walls for the lantern. Okabe-Ito Bluish Green #009E73 peaks at about 0.34 in linear light and Blue #0072B2 at about 0.45, so both sit near the threshold and flicker under vignetting (relevant once 3 or 4 teams exist).
issues.fix: Redefine every 'Night' skin as bright-field art: a white or bright background with saturated colour, with the night feel from motifs and not from darkness. Put HUD, text and score zones in the detector's setIgnore rects, or draw them bright. Draw Pit Stop and reveal silhouettes as saturated colour fills, or pause vision during them. Add team colours, emblems and borders to the existing palette brightness test. Do not use Okabe-Ito green or blue for projected team colours.

issues.where: Section 13 backlog vs Section 1, Section 14, Section 16 decision 4
issues.problem: The owner is asked to accept a Founder build on 18 Dec to 5 Jan, which is item 9 at 24.5 dev-days. That scope leaves out items 10 to 13: Ghost Caravan (the free tier and demo), run-it-back and act-break votes, awards, Moonrise, Predict and Test, and the privacy notice, KSA classification paperwork and counsel check. Section 14 says to get a local-counsel opinion before taking KSA or UAE money, and the UAE child-safety law is fully enforceable from Jan 2027. The pricing in SAR and AED implies taking that money. Pillar 6 ('an honest one more?') is also missing from the paid build. Taking the doc's own full scope to item 13 gives about 3 to 24 Jan before any slippage. There is no contingency anywhere.
issues.fix: Re-cut the Founder scope so it includes the privacy notice and the counsel check (or sell in Kuwait only until they are done), Ghost Caravan, and the run-it-back vote. Move items 10 to 13 ahead of the Day-1 date, or state the real date. Add 20 to 30% contingency. Present the owner with two dated options: 'Kuwait-only Express Founder' and 'full Founder'.

issues.where: Section 4 simulation table and Section 1 'Fairness'; rule 2 'Coach has no scoring power'
issues.problem: The 50.2 / 50.0 / 50.3 / 49.9 result follows from the model's structure. Capping both teams at S active seats makes the active head-count identical, so the sim cannot show anything else. It says nothing about the race format, which was not simulated (the doc admits this). Its own sensitivity is about 3 points of win rate per 1% of Coach effect. A Coach is physically in the tent. They can talk, point, see the lane view and use the ping. spotterScoreEffect = 0 is a config value, not something the room can enforce. On a 4v3 split only the bigger team has a free-handed Coach. If loafing depends on total team size, the doc's own numbers give 42% or 34% for the bigger team.
issues.fix: Relabel the table as 'head-count symmetry check, not evidence for the Leg'. Give the smaller team's Pilot the same ping button so the ping does not depend on having a spare person. Keep the Coach's information no richer than what the seated players see. Instrument the real metric: normalised team-time ratio per leg, bigger vs smaller, against 4v4 control rooms. Add Coach-talk to the P1 observation sheet.

issues.where: Section 15 kill criteria, Fairness row
issues.problem: The trigger is 'bigger team's win rate or per-capita output outside 40-60% across the uneven rooms' after 6 to 10 rooms. With a fair coin that band is almost never met. At 8 rooms only exactly 4 wins fall inside it, so a perfectly fair game fails about 73% of the time. At 6 rooms it fails about 69% of the time, and at 10 rooms about 34%. The doc's own per-room standard deviation of about 28 points makes this worse. The criterion will switch on the size correction spuriously. The correction is capped at plus or minus 2%, which the doc's own sensitivity puts at about 6 points of win rate, so it cannot fix a real bias either.
issues.fix: Use a continuous per-leg measure (team-time ratio across all legs, not room wins), with 4v4 rooms as controls. Pre-register a gross-failure rule only, for example 'bigger team loses or wins more than 75% of at least 12 uneven rooms, or the CI on the time ratio excludes 1 by more than 10%'. Never auto-enable the correction from room win counts.

issues.where: Section 2 timeline ('Peer-voted awards (Most Improved, Early Bird, Sharp Eyes) pay a flat 50 points') vs Section 6; Section 4 scoring
issues.problem: This is a contradiction and a fairness hole. Section 6 says the camera measures Most Improved and Early Bird, and Section 2 says they are peer-voted. If votes are per head, the bigger team has more voters, which brings back the size advantage the structure removes. 50 points is about half a leg (a leg is about 100 points), so awards can decide the result. This conflicts with pillar 3 ('fair by structure'). A popularity vote among children is also a social-pressure mechanic.
issues.fix: Compute awards from game state only. Make them cosmetic or recap-only, or cap the points at 10 or less. If any vote stays, count one vote per team, not per head, and do not let people vote for their own team.

issues.where: Section 2 Curtain Call ('The wall shows each player's before and after: Sara 7.2 s to 3.4 s'); Section 3 step 3 ('Ratings are never shown'); Section 6
issues.problem: Three problems. First, it contradicts 'ratings never shown', because the Light Check time is the rating. Second, it publicly ranks children and elders on a projected wall, and some of them will regress (Grandpa 4.0 s to 5.2 s). The doc's own cited evidence (Gerling 2014) says explicit comparisons lower self-esteem. Third, 'Most Improved' rewards a bad baseline, so kids will sandbag. The 2x cap and 'best of two tries' limit it but do not remove it. The Light Check window is 8 s, so many first tries are censored at 8 and the before/after numbers carry little information.
issues.fix: Show only positive deltas or team-level totals on the wall. Put individual times on the player's own phone. Make Most Improved cosmetic. Do not show regressions.

issues.where: Section 6 and pillar 5 'Skill you can see in 20 minutes'
issues.problem: The claim overstates what the measurement shows. The before/after uses the same two ring targets within 20 minutes, so it mostly shows task familiarity and recovery from nerves. Three of the four metrics are fragile on this detector. Steadiness (frame-to-frame jitter) is dominated by detector noise: hysteresis, a 2-frame debounce, despeckle and a 20 Hz poll. IoU of at least 0.6 on a thin ring is very sensitive to a 1 to 2 cell edge error. Times are censored at 8 s. The sandbagging guards add complexity without fixing validity. No test-retest reliability has been measured.
issues.fix: Keep the claim to 'faster and steadier at this game's shadow tasks'. Use filled shapes with coarse IoU. Compute steadiness on a smoothed centroid, not on the mask. Make Curtain Call use new but equivalent targets, not repeats of the opening ones. Add a P0 step where the owner repeats the same target 10 times to measure noise. Do not ship the before/after screen until that noise is known.

issues.where: Section 3 step 1 (age tap kid/teen/adult), Section 5 Pit Stop tiers, Section 7, Section 11 age bands
issues.problem: The knowledge tiers have no input path. The join tap has 3 options, so a 4-year-old and a 12-year-old are both 'kid'. Section 11 and Section 5 need a pre-reader tier (two pictures) and a kid tier (3 to 4 options). Section 7 says the tier comes from the age tap, not the rating, and drift is off at launch. An unknown tap has no defined tier, although it has a rating prior. Tier by age is not tier by knowledge: an adult weak on wildlife and a 10-year-old who loves it both get the wrong tier. Noor plays on a parent's phone, so the tap and tier belong to the parent's device.
issues.fix: Add a fourth option ('little / reads little') or a per-phone 'big picture cards' switch that the parent controls. Define the unknown default (Tier 2). Allow an opt-in 'harder / easier' on the card screen. Handle shared phones explicitly.

issues.where: Section 7, Section 5 Pit Stop, Section 13 items 7 and 11, Section 10
issues.problem: The knowledge role is real but small and bolted on. Oil only softens falls: about 2 flames at 70% correct, with a flame worth a restart of about 6 s in a 60 to 100 s leg. The doc cites intrinsic-integration evidence (Habgood and Ainsworth) against bolt-on quizzes, then ships a bolt-on. The integrated pieces are late: Predict and Test is item 11, after the Founder build, and Riddle Fork is Phase 3. Content is thin. 90 launch items against about 48 cards per session gives under 2 sessions before repeats, while the research recommends about 300 verified items for launch. Verification alone is about 7.5 h at 5 min per item.
issues.fix: Pull the procedural Predict and Test into the Founder scope (it needs no question bank). Make Oil worth more, for example a flame that opens a bypass door, so knowledge visibly changes the race. Raise launch content or reuse each item across tiers and formats, and say what the real repeat point is. Do not describe knowledge as a pillar until it changes outcomes.

issues.where: Section 5 Leg, Section 15 P0, Section 12 ('3.18 s' evidence)
issues.problem: Latency, occlusion and the projector path are never specified or tested. The engine polls vision at most at 20 Hz (host/app.js) with a 2-frame debounce, so a shadow takes at least 100 ms to become solid. Add camera pipeline delay, projector processing and the README's cable or cast path, and total delay is plausibly 250 to 500 ms. Casters stand between the projector and the wall, and the camera sits near the projector (the doc says 30 degrees off-axis), so their bodies can occlude the shadows. People walking through the beam, a bumped projector (which needs recalibration) and a tent wall moving in wind all break the fixed homography. Fire flicker changes the ambient level the detector learned once at calibration. Each lane is only 80 cells wide, and a gap of 180 px is about 37% of it. 'Stopped 20 px short' is about 3 cells, close to edge jitter. P0 is run by the owner alone and measures only ring-fit. The 3.18 s 'identical time' result is a deterministic synthetic run, so it shows the physics is deterministic, not that two physical lanes are fair.
issues.fix: Extend P0: measure hand-move to lantern-collision latency from high-speed phone video, wired vs cast. Test two or more people in the beam, a lit lantern and wind on the tent wall. Set pass thresholds (for example 300 ms or less, mask flicker below a stated rate). Add a 5 s recalibration path and a 'keep out of the beam' onboarding line. Do not cite the mirrored-lane run as fairness evidence. Add a kill rule for latency, with the fallback of slow-rolling lanterns and checkpoints.

issues.where: Section 14 deferred technical decisions, Section 15 kill criteria, owner decision 3
issues.problem: Internet is assumed (owner decision 3), but the research found no coverage data for camp areas and one verdict calls 'Wahiba has none' wrong while warning that deep desert is patchy. The relay now carries Pilot inputs, the unlock check and room state. There is no connectivity test or kill criterion. The existing relay is stateless: it forwards 'in' messages to the host, and the host is authoritative. The doc moves assign(), ratings and telemetry onto the relay, which is new server state.
issues.fix: Add a connectivity row to P0 and P2: RTT to the planned relay region from a camp hotspot with 8 phones. Add a pivot line (for example more than 25% of sessions with a visible input stall). Keep the offline/LAN mode as a named follow-up with a size estimate. Consider running assign() on the host, which already holds the Light Check results, so the relay stays dumb.

issues.where: Section 3 (no choice, households off by default, 'Do not collect gender'), Section 8 Buddy Pose, Section 5 casting
issues.problem: This is the most likely GCC-specific failure. The game seats two casters side by side in a roughly 1 m lane, may assign unrelated men, women and teen girls to the same team, and offers Buddy Pose. The research's only group-size example is a 16-man all-male group, and it also describes separate men's and women's tents. The household link is off by default, is not simulated and is left to 'test with a few Gulf families'. The no-choice rule is a good fit with the owner's request. As specified, it puts the cultural workaround behind a setting few hosts will find.
issues.fix: Show an optional one-tap 'who is family? link them' step before the draw, on by default. Add a host-set 'sides' option for physical seating. Limit Buddy Pose to linked households. Make 3 to 5 Gulf-family sessions a P1 gate, not a Phase-3 check. This still keeps the owner's 'players do not choose'.

issues.where: Section 3 (re-draft, act-break shuffle, late-join moves), Section 2 'Swap tents', Section 5 rules, Section 15 'rules understood in 45 s'
issues.problem: The rule load is higher than the one the doc held against Echo Dunes. A child must grasp Caster, Pilot and Coach, rotating seats, Oil and flames, Safe vs Bold, the Moonrise boost, tent swap, the re-draft, the keep/shuffle vote and awards. The 45 s comprehension criterion is unrealistic for that list with a 4-year-old and a grandparent. The spec itself says 'being moved twice looks like a bug to kids', yet the design can move up to ceil(N/4) players after leg 1, then rebalance at boundaries, then reshuffle at the act break. The doc also says teams are 'locked inside an act'.
issues.fix: Hide everything except the seat rule in the first Founder build: no visible Moonrise, no size correction, no re-draft (or move nobody after leg 1 unless the J gain is large). Write a 3-sentence rule script and time it with the P1 families. Add rules back one at a time.

issues.where: Section 13 backlog estimates and omissions
issues.problem: The estimates look optimistic and the plan has gaps. Item 2 (teams module) is 4.5 days, but the team-balance spec's own estimate is 6.5 days, or about 5.5 with the reference code. The seeded composer, 6 modules, checkpoints, Oil and 2 tuned courses are 3.0 days, and the repo requires a scripted solution per level plus a proof that the level cannot be cleared without its mechanic. A procedural composer needs an automatic solvability and shadow-necessity checker. Several promised features have no backlog line: Camp Log and Tonight's Course, ranks, badges and cosmetic skins, the printable prop PDF, the household link, host swap, the telemetry endpoint, Express Night, hosting, domain and HTTPS, the Coach UI, opt-in assists, and the course verifier. The owner's non-coding hours (P1 and P2 sessions, reviewers, the demand poll, trademark search, marketing clips) are not counted in the 12 to 15 h a week.
issues.fix: Add the missing lines. Reconcile item 2 with the spec. Add a composer verifier to item 4. Budget the owner's non-dev hours separately and reduce build days accordingly. Cut cosmetics, Camp Log and Tonight's Course from v1.

issues.where: Section 12, Section 9, Section 10, Section 13 items 11, 14, 15
issues.problem: Replay is overpromised. The chosen concept scores lowest of the top three on exactly the owner's goals: knowledge 4.0 and replay 5.3. The grafts that supposedly fix them are all after the Founder build (Echo Leg after a spike, Riddle Fork in Phase 3, Charades in Jan to Feb). The research says Charades is the best local fit and the camera-independent fallback. The v1 replay rests on 6 modules, 4 recipes and 2 tuned courses, with a seeded composer whose output quality is unproven. 'Tonight's Course' is built on that same composer. The decision by gates is defensible, but the doc should say plainly that v1 is a few Nights of play, not an endless loop.
issues.fix: State the v1 expectation in the owner summary (for example 2 to 3 Nights of fresh play). Replace 'run it back votes' as the only replay metric with nights per group over 3 weeks. Consider moving human-judged Charades (3 days) ahead of awards and the Camp Log, since it works even when the camera fails.

issues.where: Section 4 'What it does not fix' and spec 'Spotter must feel like a promotion'
issues.problem: At the person level the owner's complaint stays true by design. In a 4v3 room each member of the bigger team sits out one leg in four. The 'promotion' framing for a 9-year-old is untested, and Charades and Pit Stop, the rounds that give airtime back, are not all in the Founder build. For Reading B (compensate the bigger team) the design offers nothing to the bench person.
issues.fix: Give the Coach a visible, size-neutral job that both teams also have, for example calling the next module aloud. Include the Pit Stop airtime in the Founder scope. In P1 count how often the benched child asks to swap or complains. Offer the host a 'rotate coaches faster' option.

issues.where: Section 3 step 8, Section 2 timeline, Section 1 Decision summary, Section 8, Section 3 join
issues.problem: Several internal contradictions. (1) A shuffle is forced when one team wins two acts running by 25%, but a Night has two acts, so the rule can never fire. (2) The 8:30 act-break round is Charades, which does not exist until Jan to Feb, and Express Night has no break round at all. (3) The Decision summary says scoring uses 'per-capita means', but Section 4 says legs use one team clock and nothing is summed or averaged. Per-capita applies only to Charades. (4) Join uses preset nicknames only (no typing), yet the wall shows 'Sara 7.2 s to 3.4 s', Section 8 says names support Arabic, Latin or mixed script, and the Light Check needs a way to call the right person to the wall. (5) 'Seven phones scan' but Noor is on a parent's phone. (6) The spec says lanterns and fanoos appear only in a Ramadan skin, yet the lantern is the core object in the default skin and one name candidate is 'Fanoos Run'. (7) The Light Check is stated as 45 to 60 s, but pairs of 8 s on two rings means about 64 s of play for 7 players and about 2 minutes for 12, and it runs twice.
issues.fix: Remove or rewrite the dead rule. Define what the act break shows before Charades. Fix the scoring wording. Decide names: preset only, or show the preset nickname plus an avatar. Rework the join count for shared phones. Decide whether the lantern is the core object or only a Ramadan skin. Budget Light Check time per N.

issues.where: Section 9 guardrails, Section 3 act-break vote, Section 6 Camp Log
issues.problem: The engagement design is mostly clean, with a few soft spots for children. The 'Run it back?' vote is on every phone with 'shuffle highlighted by default', so a majority of kids can keep the group playing. A pre-highlighted default is a nudge. 'Tonight's Course' (a date-seeded course with a best-time board) is a play-by-appointment pattern from Zagal's dark-pattern list, even without streaks. The success metric (run-it-back votes) is shaped by the prompt itself. Cumulative ranks and skins are acceptable if they never expire.
issues.fix: Give the host the final say on 'again' and make 'stop' as prominent as 'again'. Remove the default highlight. Drop the 'Tonight' framing or keep it strictly optional and quiet. Keep ranks cumulative and non-expiring.

issues.where: Section 5 area cap, Section 6 prop sheet, Section 5 Leg
issues.problem: Shadow necessity is high in the Leg, Light Check and Predict and Test, but a board or tablet in the beam can fake a bridge. The printable prop sheet encourages pre-cut shapes. The area cap ('about 25%, A') has no stated behaviour when exceeded, so a person standing in the beam could make the lane unwinnable or silently drop real shadows. The '60 px non-solid margin', 'Bold about 5 s faster' and 8 s ping interval carry no (A) or (E) tag, though the header says all numbers are tagged.
issues.fix: Define the cap behaviour (for example per-lane, by area, with a visible warning). Tag the untagged numbers. Test the cap with a child standing in the beam.

issues.where: Section 6 'Giant vs Tiny', Section 5 Leg, Section 8
issues.problem: Physical safety and fatigue are not addressed. The 'Giant' target encourages approaching the projector lens in the dark (heat, tripping, knocking the projector and losing calibration). Four legs of 60 to 100 s each with raised arms are tiring for children and elders, though the doc offers props on sticks and seated roles.
issues.fix: Put a floor mark about 1 m from the lens. Offer a 'Giant by prop' option. Cap continuous holding time per leg or make the shapes rest on stands.

issues.where: Section 14 pricing, Section 16 decision 8
issues.problem: Price context is incomplete. The research found the local competitor Mkhmkh at KWD 3 per extra game, which the pricing never compares to. The Founder price (SAR 39) is about 63% of a Jackbox 5-game pack at the Dec 2025 Steam price (SAR 61.49, read from search summaries) for one playable mode plus about 90 trivia items. The free tier (up to 3 controllers, Ghost Caravan) cannot show the headline feature, 'the room decides your team', before purchase.
issues.fix: Include the Mkhmkh anchor. Test price with a short pre-sale. Let the free tier show a 2v2 room (4 controllers) with a time limit.

issues.where: Section 7 ('Kahoot added an Accuracy mode in 2025 for this reason'), Section 9 ('common to Apple Kids, the UAE Child Digital Safety Law and Zagal'), Section 14 operators
issues.problem: Several claims go beyond their sources. Kahoot's blog says the mode was added after user requests, and the slow-reader reason is the digest's inference. Apple Kids rules bind store apps, not a web-first PWA. The UAE law bans targeted ads and tracking beyond the authorised purpose, not every analytics call. 'Rental-camp operators already own projectors' rests on two or three listings and is not supported by the IndexBox data, which the claim check showed is annual flow and category-uncertain.
issues.fix: Reword to 'Kahoot added an Accuracy mode after user requests'. Say the store rules would apply only if wrapped as a native app. Keep operators as a hypothesis to poll, not a channel.

issues.where: Section 15 playtest plan P1/P2 vs Section 13 build order
issues.problem: The P1 build (item 5, about 20 Nov) predates the Light Check (item 6) and Pit Stop (item 7), so P1 tests teams on age priors only and cannot test the skill or knowledge pillars. P0 is the owner alone. The first test with several people and a child is P1.
issues.fix: Move a minimal Light Check (one ring, one measurement) into item 5, or accept that P1 tests only seats, rules and comprehension. Add a second people-in-beam run to P0 using family members.

verdicts.claim: The sales window is real but short. Qatar's season is confirmed for 25 Oct 2026 to 20 Apr 2027. Kuwait's 2026-27 dates are not yet announced; last season ran 15 Nov to 15 Mar. verdicts.topic: GCC winter camping (kashta) as an occasion for a projector + phone-camera shadow game: season dates, who camps, evening entertainment, camp set-up, night conditions (as of 2026-10-11)
verdicts.correction:
I found no contradicting evidence, but I could only read search-result summaries. WebFetch could not reach the three claimed sites (DNS failure), so I did not read the pages themselves. Dates confirmed:

- Qatar: the 2026-27 winter camping season runs 25 Oct 2026 to 20 Apr 2027. The Ministry of Environment and Climate Change announced it, and QNA, Qatar Tribune, Gulf Times and Marhaba all report it. Registration opened 11 Oct. Qatar's Ministry of Environment was already removing tents pitched before the official start (Raya, 7 Oct 2026).
- Bahrain: the 2025-26 season ran 5 Dec 2025 to 25 Mar 2026. The end date comes from a search summary and I did not see it on the page.
- Kuwait: the 2025-26 season ran 15 Nov 2025 to 15 Mar 2026. Earlier seasons used the same 15 Nov to 15 Mar window.

Nuances to fix in the plan:
1. Kuwait's season is officially the "spring camping season" (موسم التخييم الربيعي), not "winter". Kuwaiti and trade sources use that term, so search and marketing copy should too.
2. "2026-27 dates not yet announced" is an absence of evidence. My English and Arabic searches found no 2026-27 Kuwait announcement, but that cannot prove none exists.
3. "About 5 weeks away at the earliest" is an inference. 15 Nov is 35 days after 11 Oct, and that date comes from last season's pattern, not an announcement. Kuwait's 2025-26 licence applications opened on 15 Nov, and camps pitched before the official start are removed.
4. Dubai 1 Nov to 30 Apr is last season's validity (2025-26 and earlier). A guide dated 31 Aug 2026 says the 2026-27 application date was not announced then. Last season's applications opened 21 Oct 2025. Dubai permits are limited to UAE citizens with a Dubai-issued passport, for family use only, which narrows who the buyers are.
5. "Peak cold-weather camping is Dec to Feb" is general knowledge and I found no source for it.
6. The claim says nothing about KSA, which is a target market. I found no KSA camping-season dates for 2026-27.

It is not evidence of a mixed-age or mixed-gender group, so it is weak support for 'fit for a kids-plus-adults group game'. (b) I could not confirm 'cards or board games', 'music' or 'fire' in the two named Kuwait Times articles. 'Camping: Kuwait's favorite pastime' covers Subiya and Jal Al-Zour, solar gear and safety. The 'winter camping season revives cultural heritage' piece mentions only 'traditional games'. Fire, chestnuts and stories appear in a different Kuwait Times article. The 'demand unproven' conclusion is fair, but it is a gap in the sources, not a finding that demand is absent.

verdicts.correction:

(1) "Oman's Wahiba Sands has none" is contradicted. Several eSIM and travel guides say most organised Wahiba Sands camps get 3G/4G, and some say 4G/5G. (2) The Oman Observer article ("tents transform Oman's outdoors") appears to be a winter-camping feature on tent rental prices and amenities. It is not a coverage source. The search summary did not show it saying anything about mobile signal, and it is not evidence for "Wahiba has none".

(4) The KWD prices are shaky.

verdicts.claim: No ownership survey exists. Indirect sales data (about 72K units a year in KSA, about 2-2.4 per 1,000 people in KSA and Kuwait) points to low projector ownership among ordinary camping households, with higher ownership among rental-camp operators and premium campers. verdicts.topic: Projector and portable-projector adoption in the GCC for camping, outdoor and home use (as of 2026-10-11). Method note: WebFetch could not resolve any host in this sandbox, so every figure below comes from web-search result summaries, not from a page I opened. Prices are undated retailer snapshots.
verdicts.correction:
The IndexBox figures check out, but the conclusion drawn from them is weaker than the claim states.

Confirmed:
- IndexBox gives Saudi Arabia 2024 consumption of about 71-72K video-projector units. Its per-capita figure is 1.9-2 per 1,000, and Kuwait's is 2.4 per 1,000 (about 11K units).
- I found no household projector-ownership survey for KSA, Kuwait or the UAE. I also found no camping-specific or portable-projector sales data for these markets. This is an absence of evidence, not proof that none exists.

Wrong or overstated:
1. The figures are annual apparent consumption in 2024, a year IndexBox says shrank 15% (386K units) or 18.8% (364K units) across the GCC. They are modelled from trade and production data, not retail sales. Treat them as a flow, not the number of projectors households own.
2. IndexBox's own editions disagree. KSA is 71K in one edition and 72K in another, and 1.9 versus 2 per 1,000. The world average is given as 0.9, 1 or 6.2. The paid Saudi and Kuwait pages show only placeholders ("$X") in the free excerpts.
3. I could not confirm what the category covers. IndexBox's video-projector scope appears to use Prodcom 26403420, and I could not find its definition. Consumer mini and portable projectors, which often arrive through e-commerce, may be under-counted or lumped in with business projectors. So the "low ownership among camping households" inference rests on a figure that may not measure the relevant product.
4. The claim "higher ownership among rental-camp operators and premium campers" has no source. It is the author's inference.
5. The only survey I found points the other way, though it measures something different. An Epson-commissioned survey of KSA, UAE, Morocco, Türkiye and South Africa reports a 62% projector preference in KSA, and only 11.6% of respondents had neither used nor tried a projector. That is preference and usage, not ownership, and a projector maker commissioned it. I could only find trade-press coverage of it, and one article names different top markets. It does show that familiarity with projectors may be much higher than 2 per 1,000 implies.

The plan's safe conclusion is "ownership is unmeasured; do not assume the host owns a projector." It should not claim ownership is low, or that operators and premium campers own more. The IndexBox sales-implied ownership range is an unvalidated estimate.

CONFIRMED

Amazon SA lists an XuanPad at SAR 1,109.54 and a renewed AAXA P7 sells at SAR 1,442 (both inside SAR 899-2,500). WRONG OR MISLEADING

UNVERIFIED
- AED 469-559 for generic minis.

- Any Jarir Kuwait projector price. The search returned only Jarir Kuwait accessory and screen pages, with no projector prices.
- The Amazon.sa search-page prices. I saw only third-party aggregator snapshots, which are undated.

The plan's price-tier conclusion survives on this evidence. The exact tier boundaries should not be quoted as sourced facts.

verdicts.correction:
I could not verify or refute this claim. Every WebFetch to the three claimed sources and to Paddle and Lemon Squeezy docs failed with a DNS error (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). The web search budget was already used up, so I ran no searches. I found no contradicting evidence, but I also found no support. Nothing here comes from a source I read.

Untested parts of the claim (unknowns):
1. Whether specific merchant-of-record vendors (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, FastSpring and similar) accept KNET or mada. I did not check their current payment-method lists. Many foreign checkouts do accept Visa/Mastercard-branded cards, which could include co-badged mada or KNET-issuer cards.
2. The "about 80 percent of Kuwait online payments run on KNET" figure. It is labelled a vendor estimate. I found no independent source, such as the Central Bank of Kuwait or a market report.
3. The statement that Apple Pay in Kuwait is processed over KNET. A Checkout.com docs page titled "Apple Pay via KNET" suggests this, but I could not read it.
4. Whether a local KNET gateway needs a licence, and what Kuwait's rules would be for a foreign seller.

Wording in the claim that is too strong or unproven:
- Its conclusion that many Kuwaiti buyers may fail to pay is a hypothesis, not a finding. The claim itself recommends a test purchase.
- "Mandatory" for a local gateway holds only if that test fails. A foreign merchant-of-record seller may not need one, so check with the vendor and a lawyer.

Key claims the plan depends on:
- Critical: merchant-of-record checkouts do not accept KNET or mada directly. Check the vendor's payment-method page.
- Critical: Kuwaiti buyers' cards or Apple Pay will not work on a Visa/Mastercard-only checkout. Only a real test purchase with Kuwaiti cards settles this.
- Supporting: KNET's online share is about 80 percent. Only the order of magnitude matters, and the plan already assumes KNET is dominant.
- Supporting: a local KNET gateway needs a licence and takes time to set up. This matters only if the test fails.

Recommendation: before launch, buy from the live checkout with real KNET-only cards (and Apple Pay) in Kuwait, and do the same with mada cards in KSA. Rerun this check when web access and search are available.

What I can say without those sources is that the plan's conclusion looks sensible whatever the details turn out to be. Submitting to GAMR for KSA is cheap insurance. verdicts.claim: Ramadan 2027 is expected to start Mon 8 Feb 2027 (sighting evening of 7 Feb) and end Mon 8 or Tue 9 Mar, with Eid al-Fitr starting Tue 9 Mar or Wed 10 Mar (UAE holiday Mar 9 to 11 or 12). Official dates come only after moon sighting. Kuwait National and Liberation Days (25 to 26 Feb) and KSA Founding Day (22 Feb) fall inside Ramadan.
verdicts.topic: Culture, content rules and calendar for selling a family shadow-play co-op game in the GCC, Oct 2026 to Apr 2027
verdicts.correction:
The core dates hold up, but one detail is likely off by a day. I could not check any of the four claimed sources: the web search budget was exhausted and WebFetch failed on all four hosts (DNS error). I did not find any contradicting source, and I am citing no URLs. What follows rests on my own astronomical calculation (ephem 4.2.1) plus background knowledge, not on the cited pages.

What the calculation supports:
- Conjunction on 6 Feb 2027 is at 15:56 UTC. That is after sunset in the Gulf, so no crescent can be seen on the evening of 6 Feb.
- On the evening of 7 Feb the moon is about 22 hours old, 9 degrees from the sun and 9 degrees above the horizon at Dubai, Riyadh, Kuwait and Mecca. Odeh criterion V is roughly 3.6 to 4.2, which means visible with optical aid and possibly to the naked eye. Ramadan therefore most likely starts Mon 8 Feb. It would slip to Tue 9 Feb only if the crescent were not sighted.
- Conjunction on 8 Mar is at 09:29 UTC. At sunset the moon is about 5 hours old and 3 degrees from the sun, and sets 7 to 9 minutes after the sun. Odeh V is about -5, so it cannot be seen even with a telescope.
- A sighting-based Eid would therefore be Wed 10 Mar, after a 30-day Ramadan. A calculation-based Umm al-Qura-style Eid would be Tue 9 Mar. The claimed "9 or 10 Mar" range is right, and 10 Mar is the likelier date wherever the committee actually sights the moon.
- The weekdays are correct: 8 Feb is Mon, 22 Feb is Mon, 25 Feb is Thu, 26 Feb is Fri, 8 Mar is Mon, 9 Mar is Tue, 10 Mar is Wed.
- If Ramadan starts 8 Feb, KSA Founding Day (22 Feb, Ramadan day 15) and Kuwait National and Liberation Days (25 and 26 Feb, Ramadan days 18 and 19) all fall inside Ramadan.
- KSA Founding Day on 22 Feb and Kuwait's 25 and 26 Feb are fixed dates I know from background knowledge, but I could not recheck them this session.
